stories.text: Legendary manager Joe McCarthy, who won 1,460 regular-season games, eight AL pennants, and seven World Series in all or part of 16 seasons (1931 to May 23, 1946) at the rudder of the New York Yankees, takes over their rivals to the northeast, the Boston Red Sox, for 1948.
stories.headline: Joe McCarthy Takes Over Red Sox, Leaving Yankees Behind

image.alt: Smiling man in navy Red Sox cap and gray Red Sox jersey

stories.extract: The following are the baseball events of the year 1946 throughout the world.

stories.text: The American League Wild Card Series and National League Wild Card Series begin.
stories.headline: American and National League Wild Card Series Begin
stories.extract: The 2026 National League Wild Card Series were the two best-of-three playoff series in Major League Baseball’s (MLB) 2026 postseason to determine the participating teams of the 2026 National League Division Series (NLDS). Both Wild Card Series began on September 29, with Game 2s scheduled for September 30. NBC…

stories.text: In Game 1 of the 2026 National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park, Atlanta beat Philadelphia 5–3. In the top of the first inning, Alec Bohm doubled home Kyle Schwarber to give the Phillies an early lead. The Braves tied the game in the bottom of the second when Mike Yastrzemski singled in Ozzie Albies. Phillies starting pitcher Jesús Luzardo pitched five innings, allowing three hits and one run while striking out six batters.
stories.headline: Braves Beat Phillies 5-3 in Game 1 of Wild Card Series

image.alt: Man in red Phillies cap and 'For the Love of Philly' shirt at press conference

stories.extract: The 2026 National League Wild Card Series were the two best-of-three playoff series in Major League Baseball’s (MLB) 2026 postseason to determine the participating teams of the 2026 National League Division Series (NLDS). Both Wild Card Series began on September 29, with Game 2s scheduled for September 30. NBC…

stories.text: In Game 1 of the 2026 American League Wild Card Series at Daikin Park, Chicago beat Houston 6–3. Prior to the game, Pope Leo XIV, an avid White Sox fan, sent a supportive letter and blessed the team before their first playoff game since 2021. In the top of the first inning, Munetaka Murakami's sacrifice fly scored Sam Antonacci to give the White Sox an early 1–0 lead.
stories.headline: White Sox Beat Houston 6-3 in Wild Card Series Opener
stories.extract: The 2026 American League Wild Card Series were the two best-of-three playoff series in Major League Baseball’s (MLB) 2026 postseason to determine the participating teams of the 2026 American League Division Series (ALDS). Both Wild Card Series began on September 29, with Game 2s scheduled for September 30. NBC…

stories.text: Bobby Mitchell, 75, outfielder and designated hitter who played for the New York Yankees and Milwaukee Brewers in five seasons between 1970 and 1975, as well as the Nippon Ham Fighters from 1976 to 1979.
stories.headline: Bobby Mitchell, 75, Outfielder for Yankees and Brewers
stories.extract: Robert Vance Mitchell was an American professional baseball player. He attended Norristown High School in Norristown, Pennsylvania. He was an outfielder and designated hitter who appeared in 273 Major League Baseball games played between 1970 and 1975 for the New York Yankees and Milwaukee Brewers. He also played for…

stories.text: On September 29, 2019, the Rangers played their final game at Globe Life Park, a 6–1 win over the New York Yankees.
stories.headline: Rangers Beat Yankees 6-1 in Final Game at Globe Life Park
stories.extract: The Texas Rangers are an American professional baseball team based in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex. The Rangers compete in Major League Baseball (MLB) as a member club of the American League (AL) West Division. The team was founded as the Washington Senators in 1961, an expansion team awarded to Washington, D.C.,…

stories.text: The Philadelphia Phillies announced that manager Pete Mackanin will not manage the team in 2018. Instead, Mackanin will move to a new role in the organization as a special assistant to general manager Matt Klentak. Mackanin posted a 174–238 record for the Phillies in all of part of three seasons spanning 2015–2017.
stories.headline: Phillies Move Pete Mackanin out of Manager Role
stories.extract: Peter Mackanin, Jr., is an American former professional baseball utility player, coach, scout, and manager, who played in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the Texas Rangers, Montreal Expos, Philadelphia Phillies, and Minnesota Twins, from 1973 to 1981.

stories.text: The Oakland Athletics announced that Dr. Justine Siegal would serve as a guest instructor for their 2015 Instructional League club, making her the first female coach to be hired by a Major League Baseball organization.
stories.headline: Athletics Name Justine Siegal First Female MLB Coach
stories.extract: Justine Siegal is an American baseball coach, sports educator and the founder of Baseball For All. In 2009, she became the first female coach of a professional men's baseball team, when she worked for the Brockton Rox, in the independent Canadian American Association of Professional Baseball. In 2011, she became the…

stories.text: The Minnesota Twins relieve their longtime manager Ron Gardenhire of his duties, the team announces. A shortstop for the New York Mets from 1981 through 1985, Gardenhire has been with the Twins organization since 1988, first as a minor league manager and then for 11 years as the team's third base coach, before replacing manager Tom Kelly prior to the 2002 season.
stories.headline: Twins Relieve Longtime Manager Ron Gardenhire of Duties

image.alt: Man in red Twins cap, sunglasses, goatee, navy jacket, outdoors at baseball setting

stories.extract: Ronald Clyde Gardenhire is an American former professional baseball player, coach, and manager. He played as a shortstop in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the New York Mets from 1981 to 1985. After another year playing in the minor leagues, he served as a manager in the Minnesota Twins farm system for three years,…

stories.text: One day after the originally scheduled final day of the regular season, the White Sox, one-half game behind the Twins in the AL Central standings, are forced to make up a game with the Tigers that had previously been cancelled earlier in the season. The White Sox defeat the Tigers 8–2, forcing a one-game playoff with the Twins for the division title.
stories.headline: White Sox Beat Tigers 8-2, Force Playoff With Twins

stories.text: The Chicago White Sox clinch their first division title since 2000 with a 4-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers in the AL Central. Chicago has 96 victories, the best record in the American League, and is just the 10th team in the history of baseball to be in first place on every day of the season.
stories.headline: White Sox Win AL Central With 4-2 Victory Over Tigers
stories.extract: The American League of Professional Baseball Clubs, known simply as the American League (AL), is the younger of two leagues constituting Major League Baseball (MLB) in the United States and Canada. It developed from the Western League, a minor league based in the Great Lakes states, which eventually aspired to major…

stories.text: Major League Baseball announces that the Montreal Expos move to the Washington, D.C. area for the 2005 season. That night, the Expos play their final home game in front of 30,000+ fans. The Expos lose to the Florida Marlins 9-1.
stories.headline: Expos Move to Washington, Lose Final Home Game 9-1
stories.extract: The Montreal Expos were a professional baseball team based in Montreal. The Expos were the first Major League Baseball (MLB) franchise located outside the United States. They played in the National League (NL) East division from 1969 to 2004.

stories.text: Albert Pujols becomes the fourth hitter in the major leagues, and the first batter since Ted Williams in 1939–40, to collect more than 250 RBI in his first two seasons in the majors. Pujols drove in 257 runs in his first two campaigns. Joe DiMaggio holds the record with 292 RBI, Dale Alexander is second with 272, and Williams is third with 258.
stories.headline: Pujols Becomes Fourth Hitter With 250-Plus RBI in First Two Seasons

image.alt: Player in red Cardinals cap and white home jersey #5 at ballpark

stories.extract: Joseph Paul DiMaggio, nicknamed "Joltin' Joe", "the Yankee Clipper" and "Joe D.", was an American professional baseball center fielder who played his entire 13-year career in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the New York Yankees. Born to Italian immigrants in California, he is considered to be one of the greatest…

stories.text: Arnold Earley, 66, southpaw reliever who pitched from 1960 through 1967 for the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs and Houston Astros.
stories.headline: Arnold Earley, 66, Southpaw Reliever for Red Sox and Cubs
stories.extract: Arnold Carl Earley was an American professional baseball player and left-handed pitcher in Major League Baseball. He was born in Lincoln Park, Michigan, where he attended Lincoln Park High School.

stories.text: Against the Toronto Blue Jays at the SkyDome, Brady Anderson of the Baltimore Orioles hits his 50th home run of the season. The home run, leading off the game, breaks Frank Robinson's single-season franchise record of 49 home runs in 1966. Anderson also becomes the first player to hit 50 home runs in one season and steal 50 bases in another, having stolen 52 in 1992.
stories.headline: Brady Anderson Hits 50th Home Run, Leading off Against Blue Jays

image.alt: Close-up of a dark-haired man in a suit, outdoors with spectators.

stories.extract: Brady Kevin Anderson is an American former baseball outfielder and executive who currently serves as the hitting coach for the Los Angeles Angels of Major League Baseball (MLB). He played for the Boston Red Sox, Baltimore Orioles, and Cleveland Indians. He spent the majority of his career as a center fielder and…

stories.text: The Atlanta Braves wrap up the National League West with a 6–0 shutout of the San Francisco Giants.
stories.headline: Braves Clinch National League West With 6-0 Shutout of Giants
stories.extract: The National League West is one of Major League Baseball's six divisions. This division was created for the 1969 season when the National League (NL) expanded to 12 teams by adding the San Diego Padres and the Montreal Expos. For purpose of keeping a regular-season of 162 games, half of the teams were put into the new…

stories.text: While waiting through a rain delay, the Cincinnati Reds watch the Los Angeles Dodgers lose to the San Francisco Giants 4-3, which clinches the National League West Division for the Reds, their first Western Division title since the 1979 season. The Reds are the first National League team to lead their division wire-to-wire since the inception of the 162-game season.
stories.headline: Reds Clinch National League West as Dodgers Lose to Giants
stories.extract: The Cincinnati Reds are an American professional baseball team based in Cincinnati. The Reds compete in Major League Baseball (MLB) as a member club of the National League (NL) Central Division. They were a charter member of the American Association in 1882 before joining the NL in 1890.

stories.text: August A. Busch Jr., 90, brewery magnate who owned St. Louis Cardinals from 1953 until his death; oversaw three World Series (1964, 1967, 1982) titles and credited with keeping the Redbirds from moving to Houston by purchasing them in 1953.
stories.headline: August Busch Jr., 90, Brewery Magnate Who Owned Cardinals

stories.text: The Chicago Cubs deal eight-year veteran starting catcher and Georgia native Jody Davis to the Atlanta Braves for pitchers Kevin Blankenship and Kevin Coffman.
stories.headline: Cubs Trade Catcher Jody Davis to Braves for Two Pitchers

image.alt: Cubs catcher in pinstripes tagging runner, player wearing #17 Hernandez jersey

stories.extract: Jody Richard Davis is an American former professional baseball player and minor league manager. He was a catcher in Major League Baseball with the Chicago Cubs and Atlanta Braves from 1981 to 1990. A two-time National League All-Star, Davis won the 1986 National League Gold Glove Award.

stories.text: The Baltimore Orioles release outfielder Alan Wiggins, suspended August 31 after a failed drug test. The release ends his professional baseball career. In 1991, at age 32, Wiggins will become the first MLB player to die from AIDS, which he contracted through intravenous drug use.
stories.headline: Orioles Release Outfielder Alan Wiggins After Failed Drug Test
stories.extract: Alan Anthony Wiggins was an American professional baseball player. He was a second baseman and outfielder in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the San Diego Padres and Baltimore Orioles between 1981 and 1987. A speedy leadoff hitter, Wiggins had his best season with the pennant-winning Padres in 1984. He batted one slot…

stories.text: John Montefusco of the San Francisco Giants no-hits the Atlanta Braves 9–0 at Atlanta–Fulton County Stadium.
stories.headline: John Montefusco No-Hits Braves 9-0 for Giants
stories.extract: John Joseph Montefusco Jr., nicknamed "the Count", is an American former professional baseball player and coach. He played as a right-handed pitcher in Major League Baseball from 1974 to 1986, most notably as a member of the San Francisco Giants with whom he won the National League Rookie of the Year Award and pitched…

stories.text: Casey Stengel, 85, Hall of Fame manager who won a record ten pennants (tied with John McGraw) in 12 seasons leading the Yankees (1949–1960), capturing seven World Series titles (tied with Joe McCarthy); also managed Dodgers, Braves and Mets, applying his trademark humor to the Mets in their woeful first season; in 25 years as an MLB manager, posted a record of 1,899–1,835 (.509); in his playing days, an outfielder…
stories.headline: Casey Stengel, 85, Hall of Fame Manager With Ten Pennants

image.alt: Vintage baseball player in checked uniform and cap, holding bat, with Brooklyn-style B cap logo

stories.extract: Charles Dillon "Casey" Stengel was an American Major League Baseball (MLB) right fielder and manager, best known as the manager of the championship New York Yankees of the 1950s and later, the expansion New York Mets. Nicknamed "the Ol' Perfessor", he was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1966.

stories.text: In his penultimate game of 1973, 39-year-old Hank Aaron hammers his 713th career regular-season home run in a 7–0 victory over the Houston Astros at Atlanta–Fulton County Stadium. The victim is southpaw Jerry Reuss. The homer is Aaron's 40th of the season, and leaves him one shy of Babe Ruth's all-time record, which he will continue to pursue in 1974.
stories.headline: Hank Aaron Hits 713th Home Run, One Shy of Ruth's Record

image.alt: Aerial view of an oval, open-air stadium with a surrounding parking area

stories.extract: Henry Louis Aaron, nicknamed "Hammer" or "Hammerin' Hank", was an American professional baseball right fielder who played 23 seasons in Major League Baseball (MLB), from 1954 through 1976. Considered one of the greatest baseball players in history, he spent 21 seasons with the Milwaukee / Atlanta Braves in the…

stories.text: The Montreal Expos' Ron Hunt is hit by a pitch for the 50th time of the season.
stories.headline: Ron Hunt Hit by Pitch for 50th Time This Season

image.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a player in a New York Mets cap, smiling.

stories.extract: Ronald Kenneth Hunt was an American professional baseball second baseman. He played 12 seasons in Major League Baseball from 1963 to 1974 for the New York Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers, San Francisco Giants, Montreal Expos, and St. Louis Cardinals. Hunt batted and threw right-handed.

stories.text: The Pittsburgh Pirates blank Cincinnati 2–0 at Crosley Field (despite the Reds getting 11 hits off Bob Friend) to end the Reds' nine-game winning streak. Meanwhile, Ray Sadecki records his 20th victory as his St. Louis Cardinals defeat the Phillies 4–2 at Busch Stadium, the seventh win in the Cardinals' eight-game winning streak and the ninth loss in the Phillies' ten-game losing streak.
stories.headline: Pirates Blank Reds 2-0, End Nine-Game Winning Streak

image.credit: Blake Bolinger from Central NJ, United States

stories.extract: Crosley Field was a Major League Baseball park in Cincinnati, Ohio. It was the home field of the National League's Cincinnati Reds from 1912 through June 24, 1970, and the original Cincinnati Bengals football team, members of the second (1937) and third American Football League (1940–41). It was not the original home…

stories.text: Hank Bauer quits as manager of the ninth-place Kansas City Athletics before owner Charles O. Finley can fire him. Bauer's successor is former New York Yankees teammate Eddie Lopat. Finley will hire Bauer again in 1969 to manage his team, by then based in Oakland, and fire him that September.
stories.headline: Hank Bauer Quits as Kansas City Athletics Manager

image.alt: Three smiling men in Yankees uniforms with gloves, in a dugout

stories.extract: Henry Albert Bauer was an American right fielder and manager in Major League Baseball. He played with the New York Yankees (1948–1959) and Kansas City Athletics (1960–1961); he batted and threw right-handed. He served as the manager of the Athletics in both Kansas City (1961–62) and in Oakland (1969), as well as the…

stories.text: In Game 1 of the 1954 World Series, with the score tied 2–2 and two base runners in the eighth inning, New York Giants center fielder Willie Mays makes one of the greatest catches in history when he races back in the Polo Grounds to make an over-the-head catch of Vic Wertz' 462-foot drive.
stories.headline: Willie Mays Makes Over-the-Head Catch in Game 1 of World Series

image.alt: Black-and-white baseball game at a packed stadium with outfield wall, players and umpire

stories.extract: The 1954 World Series was the championship series of Major League Baseball's (MLB) 1954 season. The 51st edition of the World Series, it was a best-of-seven playoff that matched the National League (NL) champion New York Giants against the American League (AL) champion Cleveland Indians. The Giants swept the Series in…

stories.text: The Catch was a baseball play made by New York Giants center fielder Willie Mays on September 29, 1954, during Game 1 of the 1954 World Series at the Polo Grounds in Upper Manhattan, New York City.
stories.headline: Willie Mays Makes The Catch in Game 1 of World Series

image.alt: Worn leather baseball glove in display case with caption about 1954 catch

stories.extract: The Catch was a baseball play made by New York Giants center fielder Willie Mays on September 29, 1954, during Game 1 of the 1954 World Series at the Polo Grounds in Upper Manhattan, New York City. In the eighth inning, with the score tied 2–2, Cleveland Indians batter Vic Wertz hit a deep fly ball to center field…

stories.text: The NL race remains a dead heat as both the Dodgers (5–0, behind Don Newcombe) and Giants (3–0, behind Sal Maglie) shut out the Phillies and Boston Braves on the road.
stories.headline: Dodgers, Giants Both Shut out, Remain in Dead Heat
stories.extract: Donald Newcombe, nicknamed "Newk", was an American professional baseball pitcher who played ten non-consecutive seasons in Major League Baseball (MLB). He began his career in the Negro National League and ended it in Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB).

stories.text: The St. Louis Cardinals lose 7–2 to former Redbird Murry Dickson, now with the Pittsburgh Pirates, following a Red Munger defeat. It is Dickson's 5th win of the season against his former team. Meanwhile, the Dodgers sweep a doubleheader against the Braves, 9–2 and 8–0, moving them ahead of the Cardinals by a <small>1/2</small> game in the National League.
stories.headline: Dickson Beats Former Cardinals, Dodgers Sweep Braves

image.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a smiling man in a baseball cap and jersey

stories.extract: Murry Monroe Dickson was an American professional baseball right-handed pitcher, who played in Major League Baseball (MLB) during the 1940s and 1950s. He was known for his vast array of pitches and deliveries — one of his managers, Eddie Dyer, nicknamed him "Thomas Edison" for his inventiveness — and for the longevity…

stories.text: Only one day after getting Eddie Stanky back into their lineup after he fractured his right ankle July 8, the National League champion Boston Braves suffer another major injury. Left fielder Jeff Heath is lost for the World Series when he sustains a compound fracture of his left ankle; like Stanky's, Heath's injury comes at Brooklyn's Ebbets Field during a slide.
stories.headline: Braves Lose Jeff Heath to Fractured Ankle Before Series
stories.extract: Edward Raymond Stanky was an American professional baseball second baseman, shortstop, and manager. He played in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the Chicago Cubs, Brooklyn Dodgers, Boston Braves, New York Giants, and St. Louis Cardinals between 1943 and 1953. He was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

stories.text: The Chicago Cubs (now 97–56–1) sew up their first National League pennant since 1938, sweeping the Pittsburgh Pirates in a doubleheader at Forbes Field. In the nightcap, Chicago catcher Paul Gillespie, who slugged a home run in his debut MLB at bat on September 11, 1942, homers in his final plate appearance, ultimately becoming the first player to hit a homer in his first and last MLB regular-season at bats. (John…
stories.headline: Cubs Clinch First NL Pennant Since 1938 With Sweep
stories.extract: Forbes Field was a baseball park in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, from 1909 to June 28, 1970. It was the third home of the Pittsburgh Pirates, the city's Major League Baseball (MLB) team, and the first home of the Pittsburgh Steelers, the city's National Football League (NFL) franchise. From…

stories.text: Nels Potter throws a two-hit shutout for his 19th win and his Browns make a first-inning run stand up, enabling St. Louis to sweep a doubleheader against the visiting New York Yankees, 4–1 and 1–0, and move into a first-place tie with Detroit, which splits its twin bill against the Senators in Washington. The Tigers' Dizzy Trout (27–13) fails in his attempt to win his 28th game of 1944 in the nightcap.
stories.headline: Nels Potter Throws Two-Hit Shutout, Browns Sweep Yankees

image.alt: Man in baseball uniform and cap, grayscale, mid-1940s style, partial jersey lettering

stories.extract: Nelson Thomas Potter was an American professional baseball player and right-handed pitcher who appeared in 349 games in Major League Baseball over a dozen seasons between 1936 and 1949, most notably as a member, in 1944, of the only St. Louis Browns team to win an American League pennant. He also played for the St.…

stories.text: The Fort Custer team wins the national amateur championship of the American Baseball Congress with a 3–2 victory over a Charlotte, North Carolina, team. It's the last time the amateur World Series was held until after World War II.
stories.headline: Fort Custer Wins Amateur Title With 3-2 Win Over Charlotte

stories.text: John B. Foster, 78, sportswriter and editor of The Spalding Guide.
stories.headline: John B. Foster, 78, Sportswriter, Editor of Spalding Guide

image.alt: Man in suit seated at desk with telephone and papers, caption 'John B. Foster'

stories.extract: John Buckingham Foster was an American baseball writer, ballclub officer and sports editor.

stories.text: Cleveland wins its anticlimactic two final contests to ultimately finish one game behind Detroit, disappointing baseball fans rooting for what would have been the only "All-Ohio" World Series in baseball history; Cincinnati had already breezed to the 1940's NL title by 12 games.
stories.headline: Cleveland Wins Final Two Games, Finishes One Behind Detroit

stories.extract: The Cleveland Guardians are an American professional baseball team based in Cleveland. The Guardians compete in Major League Baseball (MLB) as a member club of the American League (AL) Central Division. Since 1994, the team has played its home games at Progressive Field. Since their establishment as a Major League…

stories.text: The second game of the double header between the Cleveland Indians and Detroit Tigers at Briggs Stadium is called after five innings due to rain. Hal Newhouser pitches all five innings for Detroit, and is the losing pitcher in his major league debut.
stories.headline: Hal Newhouser Pitches Five Innings in Losing Big League Debut

image.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a smiling man in a Detroit 'D' cap

stories.extract: Harold Newhouser, nicknamed "Prince Hal" and "Hurricane Hal," was an American professional baseball player. He played in Major League Baseball as a pitcher from 1939 to 1955, most notably for the Detroit Tigers, where he was selected for seven straight All-Star Games from 1942 to 1948. He became the first pitcher to…

stories.text: After scoring fifteen runs in the first game of a double header, the New York Yankees manage just one hit off Philadelphia Athletics pitcher Eddie Smith in the second game, losing 3–0. It is only the second time all season the Yankees are shut out (May 8).
stories.headline: Yankees, One Hit off Eddie Smith, Lose Nightcap 3-0
stories.extract: Edgar Smith was an American professional baseball starting pitcher in Major League Baseball who played for the Philadelphia Athletics (1936–1939), Chicago White Sox and Boston Red Sox (1947). Smith was a switch-hitter and threw left-handed. He was born in Mansfield Township, Burlington County, New Jersey.

stories.text: The Cubs again score in the first; however, their lead is short lived, as the Yankees score two in the bottom of the inning, and go on to win 5–2.
stories.headline: Yankees Score Two in Bottom of First, Beat Cubs 5-2

stories.text: Babe Ruth of the New York Yankees hits two homers to tie his own 1921 record of 59 home runs as the Yankees beat the Washington Senators, 15–4.
stories.headline: Babe Ruth Hits Two Homers, Ties Own Record With 59

image.alt: Sepia studio portrait of a ballplayer in pinstripes holding a bat, NY cap

stories.extract: George Herman "Babe" Ruth was an American professional baseball player whose career in Major League Baseball (MLB) spanned 22 seasons, from 1914 through 1935. Nicknamed "the Bambino" and "the Sultan of Swat", he began his MLB career as a star left-handed pitcher for the Boston Red Sox, but achieved his greatest fame…

stories.text: Future Hall of Famer Hack Wilson makes his major league debut for the New York Giants in a 5–1 loss to the Brooklyn Dodgers.

stories.text: Future Hall of Fame outfielder Kiki Cuyler makes his major league debut with the Pittsburgh Pirates. He is held hitless in three at-bats by St. Louis Cardinals pitcher Bill Sherdel.
stories.headline: Kiki Cuyler Makes Pirates Debut, Held Hitless by Sherdel

stories.text: Phillies pitcher Grover Cleveland Alexander pitches a complete game, giving up only one hit in a 5–0 victory over the Boston Braves in Boston to clinch their very first National League pennant.
stories.headline: Grover Alexander Throws Complete Game, Clinches First NL Pennant

image.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a man in a Phillies-style cap with 'P' logo and flannel uniform

stories.extract: Grover Cleveland Alexander, nicknamed "Old Pete" and "Alexander the Great", was an American professional baseball pitcher in Major League Baseball. He played from 1911 through 1930 for the Philadelphia Phillies, Chicago Cubs, and St. Louis Cardinals. In 1938, Alexander was elected into the Baseball Hall of Fame.

stories.text: The Louisville Colonels, who had finished last in 1889, clinch the American Association pennant with a 6–1 win over the Syracuse Stars.
stories.headline: Louisville Colonels Clinch American Association Pennant With 6-1 Win
stories.extract: The American Association of Base Ball Clubs, known simply as the American Association (AA), was a professional baseball major league that operated from 1882 to 1891. stories.text: Moses Fleetwood Walker, the first African-American to play in the major leagues, is released by the Toledo Blue Stockings. Walker never again played in the major leagues and the color barrier would not be broken for over sixty years.
stories.headline: Moses Fleetwood Walker Released by Toledo Blue Stockings

image.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a man in a wool jersey with a 'B' emblem.

stories.extract: Moses Fleetwood Walker, sometimes nicknamed Fleet Walker, was an American professional baseball catcher credited with being the first black man to play major league baseball. A native of Mount Pleasant, Ohio, and a star athlete at Oberlin College as well as the University of Michigan, Walker played for…

stories.text: Worcester loses again to Troy 10–7 in front of 25 fans in Worcester's last major league game.
stories.headline: Worcester Loses 10-7 to Troy in Final Major League Game

stories.extract: The Worcester Worcesters were a 19th-century Major League Baseball team from 1880 to 1882 in the National League. The team is referred to, at times, as the Brown Stockings or the Ruby Legs; however, no contemporary sources from the time exist that support the use of either name. The team played their home games at the…

stories.text: The National League issues a list of 10 blacklisted players who will require unanimous league approval for reinstatement. The reason given for the blacklisting is "confirmed dissipation and general insubordination."
stories.headline: NL Blacklists 10 Players for Dissipation, Insubordination
stories.extract: The National League of Professional Baseball Clubs, known simply as the National League (NL), is the older of two leagues constituting Major League Baseball (MLB) in the United States and Canada, and the world's oldest extant professional team sports league. Founded on February 2, 1876, to replace the National…

stories.text: The Polo Grounds hosts its first baseball game as the newly formed New York Metropolitans defeat the National Association champion Washington Nationals 4–2. Approximately 2,500 people attend the game, the largest crowd to see a game in New York City in several years.
stories.headline: Polo Grounds Hosts First Game as Metropolitans Beat Nationals
stories.extract: The Polo Grounds was the name of four stadiums in Upper Manhattan, New York City, used mainly for professional baseball and American football from 1880 to 1963. The original Polo Grounds, opened in 1879 and demolished in 1889, was built for the sport of polo. Bound on the south and north by 110th and 112th streets and…

stories.text: Boston clinches the pennant with an 8–4 victory over Hartford. Manager Harry Wright appears in his final game as a player.
stories.headline: Boston Clinches Pennant With 8-4 Win Over Hartford
